Do not expect a filename grammar for the "Other Videos" library type: "Other Videos" exists only as a selectable library type in the Add Library picker, and Plex publishes no naming or folder syntax for it, so all documented personal-media naming rules are attached to the Movies and TV Shows library types instead.
examples: Add Library type picker offers: Movies | TV Shows | Music | Photos | Other Videos
Personal videos with no common theme -> Movies library + "Personal Media" agent
Themed/serial personal videos -> TV Shows library + "Personal Media Shows" agent

rules.rule: For unrelated personal videos, place the video files directly inside one folder and name each file however you like, because Plex uses the filename verbatim as the displayed title (it parses no separators, no year token, and no bracket or brace tokens).
Add that flat folder as a Movies-type library whose metadata agent is set to "Personal Media".
examples: Library type: Movies; Agent: Personal Media; Folder: /Home Videos

rules.rule: Keep personal videos in a content location entirely separate from the regular Movies collection; never point both at the same path.
examples: /media/Home Videos   -> Movies library, Personal Media agent

rules.rule: To present themed personal videos in three levels, you must create a TV Shows-type library (not a "Home Videos" library) and use the "Personal Media Shows" agent; the library may still be given the display name "Home Videos".
examples: Library type: TV Shows; Library name: "Home Videos"; Agent: Personal Media Shows

rules.rule: Lay out home-series content in exactly three folder levels, <content root>/<Show name>/<Season name>/<episode files>, where the second-level folder name becomes the show title and the third-level folder name becomes the season.
examples: Show = Christmas, Season/Series = 2012, Episodes = Episode 1, Episode 2, Episode 3

rules.rule: Name each home-series file exactly `<Show> - s<Season>e<Episode> - <Title>.<ext>`, using a lowercase `s` and lowercase `e` joined with no space or separator between the season and episode numbers, and the three-character separator space-hyphen-space (" - ") between the show component, the season/episode component, and the title component.

Set the show component of the filename to the same string as the second-level folder name, and the season token to the same string as the third-level folder name, as the page's example does (Christmas/2012 -> "Christmas - s2012e.."); the page shows this only by example and never states it in prose.

Write the episode number zero-padded to two digits (e01, e02, e03) and the season as an unpadded 4-digit year (s2012), matching the page's only example; the page states no padding rule in prose, so treat two-digit episodes as the documented-by-example form rather than a stated requirement.
Do not rely on the trailing " - <Title>" text being shown: Plex currently labels these items "Episode 1", "Episode 2" and so on, and ignores any additional information in the filename.
examples: File "Christmas - s2012e01 - Getting Ready.m4v" displays as "Episode 1"
The words "Getting Ready" are dropped from the display title

rules.rule: To have embedded container metadata used for personal media, keep the files in a container that supports it (MP4, M4V, MOV) and, in Settings > Server > Agents, select the library type and agent, check "Local Media Assets", and drag it to the top of the source list.
examples: Containers that can carry embedded metadata: MP4, M4V, MOV
Settings > Server > Agents > (library type) > (agent) > Local Media Assets checked and first in list

rules.rule: Never include the word "sample" in a personal-media filename unless that file is 300MB or larger, because Plex automatically ignores any file whose name contains "sample" and whose size is under 300MB.
Never name any folder in a personal-media tree with the words "extras", "samples", "bonus", or "bonus disc", because folders containing those words are excluded from scanning.

Never place .dvdmedia, .iso or .img files (or other disk image formats), nor VIDEO_TS / BDMV-style sub-folders, in a personal-media library, because all disk image content is excluded before metadata matching begins.
Keep personal videos at the documented folder levels rather than in arbitrary sub-folders, because any sub-folder that does not follow the trailers/extras naming syntax is excluded from the scan.
examples: Excluded: /Home Videos/Picnic in the Park/raw footage/clip1.mov

rules.rule: To exclude extra files, create a file named exactly `.plexignore` (leading dot, no file extension, no .txt suffix) in any folder of the content location, with one glob pattern per line, `#` starting a comment line, `*` as the wildcard, blank lines ignored, forward slashes as path delimiters even on Windows, patterns without `/` matching filenames in the same directory (or anywhere in the tree if the file sits at the section root), and patterns with `/` matching relative to the containing directory; a `.plexignore` at the content-location root applies to all sub-folders.
examples: # Ignore all files with "trailer" in the name

rules.rule: A library scan walks the library's folders and all sub-folders looking for media that is new or has been removed, and pulls new or unmatched media into the library, fetching metadata for it; it is a directory-tree walk, not a flat listing of the library root.
examples: A file placed at /Movies/2024/Dune Part Two (2024)/Dune Part Two (2024).mkv is discovered by a scan of library root /Movies without any per-folder registration
A file deleted from a nested sub-folder is detected as removed by the same scan

rules.rule: After renaming a media file, moving files between locations, adding or deleting media files, or adding/removing folders from the library source, trigger Scan Library Files; Refresh Metadata is the wrong action for these changes because it updates metadata rather than detecting filesystem changes.
examples: A renamer that rewrites 'movie.2024.1080p.mkv' to 'Movie (2024).mkv' must issue a Scan Library Files against that library afterwards
Relocating a season folder from /TV/Show/S01 to /TV/Show/Season 01 requires a scan, not a refresh

rules.rule: Refresh Metadata re-fetches metadata for an item or library even when metadata already exists, so use it only for metadata concerns (agent option changes, added local media assets such as artwork, theme music or external subtitle files, bad or missing posters), never as a way to make Plex notice renamed files.
examples: Dropping Movie (2024).en.srt beside the video and wanting Plex to pick it up: Refresh
Changing the library's Metadata Agent settings: Refresh

rules.rule: Refresh All Metadata on a library performs both actions: it scans for new or changed content in the library AND re-fetches metadata for every item including those that already have metadata, so it is a superset of a scan and is correspondingly slow.
examples: Automation that only needs new files indexed should call Scan Library Files, not Refresh All Metadata, to avoid re-fetching metadata for the whole library

rules.rule: Do not depend on the 'Update my library automatically' filesystem-watch feature when the library content lives on a network share mounted via SMB, NFS, AFP or similar; it is expected to work only on local filesystems, so on a NAS-backed library trigger the scan explicitly or enable periodic updates.
examples: Library path /Volumes/media/Movies over SMB: renamer must call the scan itself
Library path /mnt/nfs/tv over NFS: enable 'Update my library periodically' as the fallback

rules.rule: When relying on automatic library updates, allow at least 60 seconds of complete drive inactivity after the last write before concluding that the automatic scan did not fire.
examples: A batch rename of 500 files: wait 60s after the final rename completes before checking whether Plex picked the changes up

rules.rule: The periodic scan frequency is chosen from a fixed set of intervals: every 15 minutes, every 30 minutes, hourly, every 2 hours, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, or daily; controlled by the 'Update my library periodically' toggle plus the 'Library update interval' setting.
examples: Worst-case latency before a renamed file appears, with periodic updates only and the interval set to daily, is roughly 24 hours

rules.rule: Periodic scan times are anchored to Plex Media Server's start time rather than to wall-clock boundaries, so the next scan is start_time + N * interval.
examples: Server started 12:15 with a 30-minute interval: scans at approximately 12:45, 13:15, 13:45, not at 12:30 and 13:00

rules.rule: The automatic and periodic library scan settings are located at Settings > Server > Library in the Plex Web App (note: this article was last modified 2019-07-31, so verify the path against the current UI).
examples: Documentation or a setup guide pointing users at Settings > Server > Library to enable 'Update my library automatically'

rules.rule: The advanced option 'Run a partial scan when changes are detected' changes what a manual action does: with it enabled, refreshing a TV series also scans for new or changed content in that series' directory, so series-level refresh behaviour is not constant and must not be assumed.
examples: Adding /TV/Show/Season 02/Show - S02E01.mkv and refreshing the series picks the episode up only when partial scan is enabled; otherwise a full Scan Library Files is needed

rules.rule: Refreshing an individual movie or TV episode scans only for new local media assets (subtitles, local artwork and the like) for that item and re-fetches its metadata; it does not scan the library for new files.
examples: Adding Movie (2024).en.srt and poster.jpg beside an existing movie file: an individual-item Refresh is sufficient
Adding a brand-new movie folder: an individual-item Refresh will not find it

rules.rule: Refreshing a music artist or album only gathers new metadata for that artist or album; no content scan is listed for this action, so new music files require a library scan.
examples: Adding a new track to an existing album folder requires Scan Library Files, not an album Refresh
